misreadings.quote: He devours the fresh food first and leaves the old cheese and the vegetables untouched.
misreadings.evidence: he consumed the cheese, the vegetables and the sauce; the fresh foods, on the other hand, he didn't like at all, and even dragged the things he did want to eat a little way away from them because he couldn't stand the smell.
misreadings.explanation: Gregor ate the old cheese, vegetables and sauce and rejected the fresh food, so the reflection reverses what happened.

misreadings.quote: finding it the only place where he felt at ease
misreadings.evidence: he hurried under the couch. It pressed down on his back a little... but he nonetheless felt immediately at ease
misreadings.explanation: The text says he felt at ease under the couch, not that it was the only place where he did.

misreadings.evidence: It was not until it was getting dark that evening that Gregor awoke from his deep and coma-like sleep... his injuries must already have completely healed as he found no difficulty in moving.
misreadings.explanation: The healing is Gregor's inference after a day and a night, and the text never says it was instant.

result.note: The main error is the reflection's reversal of which foods Gregor ate; the other two are low-severity overstatements in the prose version.
